answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through mandatory staking, where each identity must lock scarce tokens as a verifiable anchor before transacting. Viewing network requests through the prism of staked capital ensures that spinning up thousands of fake agents imposes a massive financial cost on the attacker. If malicious behavior is detected, the protocol slashes their collateral, leaving the attacker stranded on a barren knoll of sunk costs while honest participants remain secure.
